questions.q: A small plant has a thalloid body with rhizoids, is predominantly haploid, and requires water for motile male gametes to reach the female sex organ. Which group and life-cycle feature best fit these observations?
options: A) Bryophytes, with a dominant gametophytic phase
B) Gymnosperms, with an independent dominant gametophyte
C) Angiosperms, with a free-living haploid plant body
D) Pteridophytes, with no need for water during fertilisation
questions.answer: A) Bryophytes, with a dominant gametophytic phase
questions.explanation: The Exemplar describes a haploid thalloid plant with rhizoids and water-dependent motile male gametes as a bryophyte. It also states that the gametophyte is the dominant phase in the bryophyte life cycle. These two clues together identify both the group and the life-cycle emphasis.

questions.q: Which observation most strongly links certain pteridophytes with the evolutionary origin of seed habit?
options: A) Their sporophyte is always replaced by a free-living gametophyte
B) They form two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores, a condition that foreshadows the seed habit
C) Their gametophytes are always enclosed inside flowers
D) They produce endosperm by triple fusion
questions.answer: B) They form two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores, a condition that foreshadows the seed habit
questions.explanation: The Exemplar highlights heterospory, the production of microspores and megaspores, in a few pteridophytes and all spermatophytes. It specifically asks about the evolutionary significance of this feature and how it acts as a precursor to seed habit. Hence heterospory provides the relevant evolutionary bridge.

questions.q: A flowering plant has a diploid chromosome number of 36. If double fertilisation proceeds normally, what chromosome number should be expected in its endosperm?
questions.explanation: A plant with 2n = 36 forms haploid gametic nuclei with n = 18. In angiosperms, the endosperm is formed by fusion involving three haploid nuclear sets, giving 3n. Therefore the endosperm chromosome number is 3 x 18 = 54.

questions.q: A tall seed plant is diploid, bears sporophylls in compact cones, and is well adapted to extreme conditions. Which additional observation is most consistent with the same group?
options: A) Its dominant plant body is a free-living prothallus
B) Its embryo sac is always the only visible plant body
C) It must be a bryophyte because cones are haploid gametophytes
D) It belongs to gymnosperms, the same broad group that includes Sequoia
questions.answer: D) It belongs to gymnosperms, the same broad group that includes Sequoia
questions.explanation: The Exemplar uses diploidy, adaptation to extreme conditions and cone-bearing sporophylls to identify gymnosperms. It separately identifies the giant redwood Sequoia as a gymnosperm. These clues are consistent with the same plant group rather than bryophytes or pteridophytes.
